scenario: Five-year-old boy with four days of cough and runny nose, brought by his mother; mild wheeze.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hello, come in. Who do we have here?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: This is Aarav, he is five years old. Sorry doctor, we were waiting for almost one hour outside, he got very restless.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Sorry about that, we had a very busy morning. What is the problem with Aarav?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: He has a cough, mostly at night, and a running nose. He also felt warm yesterday.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: How many days?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Five days. No, wait, today is Thursday, it started on Sunday, so four days. Yes, four days.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Is he vomiting or refusing feeds? Any rash?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No vomiting, and he is eating fine. No rash.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Did you give him anything at home?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Dolo syrup when he was warm, and some cough syrup from the chemist near the school. I do not know the name, it was a red colour.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Does he have any allergies to medicines?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: He is not allergic to any medicine. But dust makes him sneeze a lot.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any previous chest problems?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: He had pneumonia when he was two, and he was in hospital for three days. And his father has asthma.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Okay. His temperature is 99.4 now. His oxygen is 98 and he is breathing twenty four breaths a minute, which is fine for his age.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: At night he was breathing fast also, and I got scared. I am worried it is pneumonia again.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let me listen. His throat is a little red, his ears are normal, and there are a few wheezes on both sides of the chest, but no crackles.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Is it serious?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: It does not look like pneumonia. I think this is a chest infection with some wheeze, possibly the start of asthma, but we cannot say that yet.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: What medicine will you give?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Salbutamol syrup, five millilitres three times a day for five days, and saline nose drops before sleep. Use the dolo only if he feels hot again.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Do we need to do any tests?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Not now. If he is not better in five days, or the breathing gets faster, we will do a chest x-ray.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: What about school? He has a unit test on Monday.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Keep him at home till Monday. Give plenty of fluids, keep his head a little raised when he sleeps, and keep him away from dust and smoke. Bring him back on Monday for a check.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay doctor, thank you very much.

gold.key: had pneumonia when he was two
a few wheezes on both sides
keep him at home till monday
keep his head a little raised

notes: Paediatric consultation: the Patient speaker is the child's MOTHER speaking about the child (the doctor addresses her as the carer). All symptoms and history belong to the child. Waiting-time and school remarks (turns 1, 2, 23) are unlabelled small talk. Self-correction in turn 5 (five days, then four days): gold is four days. The cough syrup in turn 9 is unnamed and therefore labelled uncertain. Dust sensitivity in turn 11 is an environmental allergy (not a drug allergy) and is labelled as allergy; this is a borderline label. Turn 18 includes a negated assessment (does not look like pneumonia) and two hedged ones. Doctor prescribes salbutamol and nose drops (new) and tells the mother to use dolo only if needed (already used).
